instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: A Serie A season, not English: a 21-year-old starting for the Inter side that won the record Scudetto, already an Italy international. Rated on that evidence, which is thinner than the English seasons.
First-choice holding midfielder for Real Madrid and France at twenty-four — the destroying and the covering were elite, everything in front of the ball was not.
The treble season, and UEFA’s best player in Europe for it: genuinely in the argument for the best attacking player in the world that year.
Almost the whole of his output arrived from twenty-five yards; a limited player with one genuinely top-flight weapon.
His breakthrough season: an ever-present whose direct running drove Wigan's late escape from relegation, and it earned him a move to Chelsea.
Arrived in January at 19 for £17m and was immediately a difference-maker in short bursts; the ceiling is higher than the season, but the season is already good.
His best English season: the outstanding attacking player in the league for the first three months before a run of injuries and a loss of nerve turned it.
A twenty-eight-game regular on Newcastle's return: tall, organised, and with nothing on the ball above the lower half of the division.
Liverpool's player of the season in a bad Liverpool year: a Portugal regular who covered enormous ground and scored five from deep.
A first European season spent adapting, but the engine and the ball-carrying were already there; short of the player he was by 2014.
Fully settled in his second season. He was one of Chelsea's best players in a year when they were often poor, with the running and the big goals to show for it.

The best player in a relegated side, which the spec warns against over-rating — but the ball-carrying and passing were genuinely above the division, so 75 rather than the 80 his reputation that season suggests.
Physically well up to the level and a capable defender; the temperament cost his sides more than the defending won them.
A Dutch international and UEFA Cup winner with Feyenoord arriving at 33; rated as an intelligent but slowing holding midfielder, not on the reputation.
The best defensive midfielder outside the top four that season — he broke up play against anybody and kept the ball simply. Newcastle's finish says nothing about him.
Twenty-five and an established starter in the best defence in the world; short of his own peak.
A January arrival from Paris and immediately the most inventive footballer at the club — beat his man at will, if not always usefully.
City’s best player in his first season: a Brazil international with genuine technique and a dead ball worth a goal a month.
A long way from the player of 1990-96 — unfit and immobile — but the touch, passing and game intelligence were still above anything else in that midfield.
Continued decline at thirty-two; seven starts of a player close to finished.
Final top-flight season at 34. Almost none of the peak athleticism or drive survives; the touch and vision do, which is what keeps him above the bottom of the scale.

Rated on ability, not on the flop narrative: a two-time Serie A footballer of the year and Argentina’s first-choice midfielder, with elite passing range and power. His Premier League output was poor; the footballer was elite.
A five-point drop: repeated injuries at Chelsea reduced him to five starts and he never regained the physical level of his United seasons.
Never kicked on after the teenage breakthrough; pace without a finished game.
